summary: A white reinforced-concrete light and fog signal at the end of a third-of-a-mile breakwater, lit in 1913 to guide ships into Superior's harbour; automated in 1970 and now privately owned.

access.note: Tower closed; reached only along the Army Corps of Engineers' breakwater from Wisconsin Point. Ownership unsettled in sources (2026).

facts.agency: Coast Guard owns the navigation equipment; building offered by GSA 2024, called privately owned by the Coast Guard in June 2026

notes_for_editor: Record's range_nm 13 vs NRHP 'visible for 22 miles' (unit unstated): range left out of facts. Aerobeacon 1970 is DCB-25 (NRHP) vs DCB-24 (LF, USLHS). Fog signal start 27 Aug (NRHP) vs 15 Oct (LF) 1893; one 6-inch whistle (LF) vs a pair (NRHP). Minnesota Point light 1856 (NRHP) vs 1858 (LF). Ownership today is unclear: GSA reoffered it 2024 and six groups applied (outcome not found), but Coast Guard releases of June 2026 call it 'privately owned' (Broudy's 2019 sale reportedly fell through; whether a later private purchase happened is unverified). Beacon theft ~13 May 2026; current light status unknown. Roster = USLHS archive (cites [9]); people with 1960s service named only in public roles. The Peter E. Jones 'ghost' account is from Lighthouse Digest 2010 via Lighthouse Friends; unnamed in story. USLHS place record says old Wisconsin Point (Superior Entry) light and fog building discontinued 1913 (snippet only; not in cached page). Newspaper search (Chronicling America, WI 1914, Campbell rescue) returned nothing; Lighthouse Board reports 1902-1912 not in corpus, so the 1905 storm and 1897-1902 lights rest on NRHP/LF. Record staffing/agency says USCG; Putnam page 162 per its index. Lat/lon fine (46.7101,-92.0064). Fact-check 2026-10-27: 'south pier longer' is NRHP (1880s works), not 'early 1890s'; Board's FY1894 report (scan p.311) supports the single 6-inch whistle on 15 Oct 1893 and (scan p.525) says the keeper's dwelling was 'transferred' to the Wisconsin side while LF says a duplex was built; unresolved. LF dates the rear pole light 1898, NRHP 30 Nov 1897. 'Privately owned' is InForum's wording of a Coast Guard release, not in WPR. Putnam printed page 162 unconfirmed (scan 217).
